question.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)+2g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ \frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{t} \\ \frac{{t}^{2}+4}{t-2}\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}2t-2 \\ \frac{4t-1}{{t}^{2}-1} \\ {4}^{t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of $f(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}2{e}^{t} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{t} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{{t}^{2}+4}{t-2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{0} \\ 0 \\ \frac{{0}^{2}+4}{0-2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The limit of a second component here was found using L'Hopital's Rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{t} & ={lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{′}}{{t}^{′}} \\  & ={lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{1} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡0}{1} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the limit of $g(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t)=[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}(2t-2) \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{4t-1}{{t}^{2}-1} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}{4}^{t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2(0)-2 \\ \frac{4(0)-1}{{0}^{2}-1} \\ {4}^{0}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)+2g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)+2{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+2[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
